argv:
Task: infer-pattern; case: widget-code.

Infer the hidden string rule from the labelled visible examples in input.json. Return a Python regular expression, evaluated with re.fullmatch, which describes the entire string. Anchors are optional. Do not simply list the accepted examples: grading uses a separate held-out set. You may test a candidate on the visible examples. The pattern must be nonblank, have no surrounding whitespace, and contain at most 120 characters. The verifier also rejects a group containing a quantifier when that group is itself quantified with *, +, or a counted repetition. The hidden rule and held-out examples are not supplied.

Read input.json using any available tools. Work efficiently; no particular tool or full-data display is required. Do not modify input.json or prompt.txt. Write only the final answer object to answer.json, then stop. Use these exact fields and types; do not add fields.

Answer JSON Schema:
{"type":"object","properties":{"case":{"type":"string","enum":["widget-code"]},"pattern":{"type":"string"}},"required":["case","pattern"],"additionalProperties":false}

Let me analyze. Accepted:
- AB-123 (2 letters, dash, 3 digits)
- ZZ-000
- QT-456-R (2 letters, dash, 3 digits, dash, R)
- MN-789
- XY-001-R

Rejected:
- A-123 (1 letter)
- ABC-123 (3 letters)
- AB-12 (2 digits)
- AB-1234 (4 digits)
- ab-123 (lowercase)
- AB-123-X (X instead of R)
- AB123 (no dash)
- AB-123-R-R (extra)

So pattern: two uppercase letters, dash, three digits, optionally dash R.

Pattern: [A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{3}(-R)?

Let me verify all. AB-123-R matches optional. Good.

Check no nested quantifier issues. Fine.
